current_answer: As of 24 October 2026, public evidence reviewed here still does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. A fresh Claude Code report describes poor, repetitive Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 responses in a long VS Code session with context compaction, including bad client-call advice; it is one user account without matched outputs or independent replication. Anthropic status records separate resolved error windows from 21 to 24 October. The 21 October Fable 5 event may overlap the report, but the issue gives no exact UTC time, so causation is unknown. A new 22-probe BenchGecko index marks GPT-6.1 Sol Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 stable on its 21 October run; that narrow panel does not test long conversations or agent workflows. Recent ChatGPT state and refusal reports remain separate one-user leads. Before switching, preserve the task and error, check status, then replay a safe synthetic task after recovery with model, client, effort, context, and compaction state recorded.

catalogue_card.question: Is a poor AI answer a model problem—or a bad service window?
catalogue_card.text: A Claude Code user reports costly advice and correction loops, while Anthropic lists several resolved model-error windows. The issue’s test time is unknown, so the overlap is a lead—not a cause.

summary: Broad capability decline across popular AI models is not established.
One Claude Code / VS Code issue reports poor and repetitive Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 behavior during long sessions with context compaction; it is not independently replicated.

Anthropic lists separate, resolved service-error windows for selected Claude models between 21 and 24 October. The 21 October Fable 5 incident may overlap the issue date, but the author supplied no UTC time; status is not completed-answer evidence.
A 24 October OpenAI Community follow-up reports the Chat memory full banner returning in new chats. It blocks sending and is separate from answer quality.
BenchGecko’s 21 October 22-probe index labels GPT-6.1 Sol Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 stable in its narrow test; this does not test multi-turn customer work or context compaction.
The 23 October GPT-6 regular-versus-Temporary Chat comparison and a separate Codex refusal-loop report remain individual, surface-specific leads.
Save the output or error, check status, then test a safe synthetic task after recovery. Record model, client, effort, context and compaction; change one variable at a time.
Analytics were unavailable; reader discovery, actions, repeat use, switching and commercial outcomes remain unmeasured.
uncertainty: The Claude Code issue is one user account with no matched response archive, verified served route, or independent replication.
The Anthropic status record for 21 October and the issue share a calendar date, but the issue gives no test time or time zone; a causal link is not established.
Anthropic status windows describe provider-reported errors and recovery; they do not measure completed answer quality or prove every account recovered.
BenchGecko’s 22-probe monitor is narrow, uses a judge model on some refusal questions, and does not recreate context-compacted conversations or an agent workflow.
The Chat memory full report is a single user follow-up, not an official diagnosis or model-quality measurement.
The earlier GPT-6 regular-versus-Temporary Chat and Codex refusal comparisons involve individual reports, not population estimates.
The read-only analytics broker was unavailable, so readership, repeat use, switching, and revenue remain unknown.
freshness_note: Reviewed 24 October 2026. A new Claude Code workflow complaint and multiple resolved provider error windows add a cross-provider test lead; status timing does not identify the cause, and broad decline remains unproven.
